sections.title: Habit and habitat
sections.text: Combretum micranthum, kinkéliba, is a shrub or small tree of West Africa, often 2–4 m tall; it can also climb as a liana. Its leaves are opposite or in whorls of three, and its cream flowers are grouped in spikes. It grows in dry savanna and on stony or degraded soils.

sections.title: Leaves and infusion
sections.text: The dry fruit is a reddish-brown, four-winged nut about 1.2–1.5 cm long. The leaves are traditionally infused as a drink; this cultural use is not a therapeutic recommendation. The plate matches the leaves, pale flowers and winged fruits.
